steps.title: What Is a Visual Pipeline?
steps.text: A visual pipeline is a data processing workflow represented as a DAG (Directed Acyclic Graph). You build pipelines by dragging nodes onto a canvas and connecting them, without writing code.

steps.title: Node Types
steps.text: Pipelines use five node types: Source nodes read data, Transform nodes filter and map, Sink nodes write output, Branch nodes split flows, and Merge nodes combine flows back together.

steps.title: Connections and DAG Patterns
steps.text: Nodes are connected with directed edges that define data flow. The DAG structure ensures data flows in one direction with no cycles. Lesson 25.4 covers fan-out, fan-in, and parallel processing patterns.

steps.title: Node Palette and Configuration
steps.text: Each node has a configuration panel where you set topics, serializers, filter expressions, and positions. The visual editor validates your pipeline before execution to catch errors early.

steps.title: Running and Monitoring Pipelines
steps.text: Once built, pipelines can be started, monitored in real time, and debugged with data flow inspection. Lesson 25.5 covers monitoring throughput, debugging data issues, and troubleshooting.
